newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bridgestone asks for offers, nearby trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Bridgestone asks for offers, nearby trade thin.

text.p: Bridgestone sought offers in the market on Monday for SIR20 rubber but no deals were concluded as the Singapore rubber market endured another day of lacklustre trade, dealers said.
"Bridgestone was asking around again for SIR20 rubber," a dealer for a European rubber trading firm said.
"They were looking for something between 50-51 (U.S.) cents (a kg). But nothing was done," a Singapore-based dealer said.
Traders said the company was probably hoping to attract offers below 50 U.S. cents a kg. "But I don't think anyone will be offering them below those levels," another dealer said.

Trading in the local market remained flat, dealers said. "There's nothing that has been done on the nearby months. We have also not been able to do anything for TSR20 rubber," a dealer said. "The volume today is really thin."
At around 0945 GMT, the June RSS3 contract was seen unchanged at 121.00 U.S. cents a kg.

May RSS1 was indicated steady at 173.50 Singapore cents (US$1.20) a kg. May TSR20 was indicated unchanged at 161.75 Singapore cents (US$1.12) a kg. October/December TSR20 was seen also steady at 118.00 U.S. cents a kg.
